payout_quote: Official Zazzle Help: 'Creators earn Royalties from sales of their published Products and Content. Creators may set their Royalty rate anywhere between the Standard Royalty Rate and the Maximum Royalty Rate.' Name Your Royalty Table: Physical Products — Standard 5%, Maximum 50%; Digital Products — 5% to 99%. And: 'For physical Products, we recommend setting Your Royalty Rate between 5% and 10%.' 'If you set Your Royalty Rate above 10%, an Excess Royalty Fee of 5% (of your Gross Royalty) will be applied.'
steps: Create a free Zazzle account and open your store.
Upload designs; create products; set your royalty rate (5%-50% physical, up to 99% digital).
Publish products; Zazzle handles production, sales, and shipping.
Earn royalties per sale at your chosen rate (minus fees if applicable).
catches: Higher royalty rates raise the product price, which can reduce sales — Zazzle recommends 5%-10% for physical products to stay competitive.
A 5% Excess Royalty Fee applies to royalties above a 10% rate.
Marketing royalty fees may be deducted if sales come through Zazzle's marketing or ambassador links.
Highly variable; most creators earn little; income depends on designs and traffic.
biggest_catch: You choose your royalty rate, but Zazzle warns that rates above 10% trigger a 5% excess fee and higher prices can kill sales — so the practical earning rate for physical products is 5%-10% of each sale, with no guaranteed volume.
eligibility: 18+; original content you have rights to.
timing: Royalties paid per Zazzle's payment schedule.
